name: Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage payroll compliance (construction/gov contractors)
note: Penalties + debarment are dollar-denominated pain a buyer has already felt. Jurisdiction-specific wage determinations = regulatory moat a horizontal tool won't replicate. Contractor associations = named channel.

name: Estate planning & probate document automation
note: You have lived founder-market fit. $2-5k/family cost is quantified. Moat capped at 3: Trust & Will exists and frontier models draft documents; state-specific probate rules help but UPL (unauthorized practice of law) risk means the safe buyer is attorneys/paralegals, not families.

name: Cross-border regulatory compliance for SME importers/exporters
note: Strongest moat on the list (multi-jurisdiction regulatory logic) but the build is huge for a solo founder: HS codes, sanctions lists, origin rules. Sanctions screening carries liability. Horizon Europe eligibility for a US solo founder is unverified.

name: Fire & building code compliance review for architects/engineers
note: Real per-project ROI, but building codes are copyrighted (ICC); UpCodes spent years in litigation over exactly this. Content licensing is a hidden cost and legal risk.

name: Special education IEP documentation & compliance for schools
note: 10 hrs/wk quantified pain, real regulatory moat (IDEA/FERPA). Velocity 2: district procurement is annual-budget-cycle; student data triggers heavy trust-pack burden early. A teacher-direct wedge could raise velocity.

name: Food safety recall traceability for food manufacturers
note: FSMA 204 enforcement has been pushed out (verify current date; last known ~2028), which softens urgency. Manufacturers buy slowly; recall insurance partnership is a later-stage play.

name: Invoicing & payment recovery for trades
note: Real pain, reachable buyer, but Jobber/Housecall Pro already own the invoice and can ship a collections feature in a quarter. Payments handling adds billing complexity and possible money-transmission issues at MVP.

name: Predictive maintenance for SMB manufacturers
note: Needs sensor data; without hardware you're a dashboard on data SMBs don't collect. Capital 1 = hardware-adjacent build. Wrong shape for a solo software founder.

name: Construction scheduling & bid automation
note: ALICE raised $61M and this is their core; scheduling optimization is a deep-tech build. Buyer is an enterprise GC with committee procurement. Wrong weight class for a solo founder.

name: Supply chain disruption early warning for mid-market
note: Value = data aggregation breadth, which is exactly what Resilinc/Everstream and frontier models with web access already do. Hard to defend.

name: Senior care coordination & fall risk assessment
note: Fall-risk assessment edges toward software-as-medical-device territory; care facilities are slow, liability-sensitive buyers. Emotional buyer is not the same as budget-holding buyer.
